title: “their own prophets” (1 Thessalonians 2:15) — Tischendorf’s Greek has no word for “own”
summary: KJV 1 Thessalonians 2:15 says those who killed the Lord Jesus also killed “their own prophets”. The Textus Receptus text served prints τους ιδιους προφητας; Tischendorf’s text prints τοὺς προφήτας, without ἰδίους [own].
text: KJV 1 Thessalonians 2:15: “Who both killed the Lord Jesus, and their own prophets, and have persecuted us; and they please not God, and are contrary to all men:” Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) 1 Thessalonians 2:15: τῶν καὶ τὸν κύριον ἀποκτεινάντων Ἰησοῦν καὶ τοὺς προφήτας, καὶ ἡμᾶς ἐκδιωξάντων, καὶ θεῷ μὴ ἀρεσκόντων, καὶ πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις ἐναντίων, Greek New Testament (Textus Receptus as served, printed there without accents) 1 Thessalonians 2:15: των και τον κυριον αποκτειναντων ιησουν και τους ιδιους προφητας και ημας εκδιωξαντων και θεω μη αρεσκοντων και πασιν ανθρωποις εναντιων Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/52/2/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/52/2/.
reasoning: The KJV “their own” renders ἰδίους, present in the TR text and absent from Tischendorf’s. Without it the Greek says “the prophets”, with no statement that they were the prophets of the same people as the killers.
scope: T applies at 1 Thessalonians 2:15 only. The difference is between Greek editions: the Textus Receptus text served agrees with the KJV and Tischendorf’s text does not. This record does not say which reading is original, and two digital editions are not a survey of manuscripts. title: “be at peace among yourselves” (1 Thessalonians 5:13) — Tischendorf’s Greek has “among them”
summary: KJV 1 Thessalonians 5:13 ends “be at peace among yourselves”. The Textus Receptus text served prints εν εαυτοις [among yourselves]; Tischendorf’s text prints ἐν αὐτοῖς [among them, or among themselves].
text: KJV 1 Thessalonians 5:13: “And to esteem them very highly in love for their work’s sake. And be at peace among yourselves.” Greek New Testament (Tischendorf, eighth edition) 1 Thessalonians 5:13: καὶ ἡγεῖσθαι αὐτοὺς ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ ἐν ἀγάπῃ διὰ τὸ ἔργον αὐτῶν. εἰρηνεύετε ἐν αὐτοῖς. Greek New Testament (Textus Receptus as served, printed there without accents) 1 Thessalonians 5:13: και ηγεισθαι αυτους υπερ εκπερισσου εν αγαπη δια το εργον αυτων ειρηνευετε εν εαυτοις Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/TISCH/52/5/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/TR/52/5/.
reasoning: With ἑαυτοῖς the command is to the readers to keep peace with one another; with αὐτοῖς it can read as peace with the leaders named in the previous clause (αὐτούς, “them”, at the start of the verse). The two editions therefore give different people for the peace.
scope: T applies at 1 Thessalonians 5:13 only. The Greek pronoun αὐτοῖς can also be read as “among yourselves” in some contexts; this record does not say which sense Tischendorf’s reading carries.
